payload.summary: Two Firefox failures survive the 2026-09-20 triage: the document-viewer hit counter and the tools Forms panel, both a click whose state change never lands
payload.detail: Read the Playwright trace from the failing run BEFORE proposing any fix; playwright.config.ts sets trace: retain-on-failure so it exists, and its After-DOM snapshot of the click answers this in minutes. THE TWO: (1) ui-smoke.spec.ts "search regressions avoid fetch errors and open viewer hits @critical" - after clicking Next document search hit, "Hit 2 of 2" never appears (element NOT FOUND, not hidden); (2) ui-tools.spec.ts "tool links point to the expected in-app modes" - the Forms complementary panel resolves to zero elements, on the 4th of 6 loop passes, while Services with an identical /?mode=<id> href passes. SAME SHAPE, so probably one shared Firefox cause. RULED OUT by two independent agent reads, do not re-derive: text split across elements (Playwright elementText flattens descendants and JSX/SSR comment separators); a collapsed <details> or any CSS cause (a hidden node still matches, and would report hidden not not-found - no stylesheet removes a node from the DOM); scrollIntoView/smooth scroll (suite-wide reducedMotion: reduce makes resolveScrollBehavior return auto); keyboard/focus; a click intercepted by the fixed composer (Playwright's hit-target interceptor blocks and retries, failing AT the click); Forms-specific data or markup (tools-catalog.ts Forms and Services are the same shape, and DetailActions renders the href link unconditionally). LEADING CANDIDATES: for (1), the handler firing zero times or twice - with exactly 2 hits, (i+d+2)%2 returns to 0 either way - with the exclusive-accordion open-attribute fight at source-panels.tsx:1063 as a plausible Gecko-specific trigger; for (2), the panel's hardcoded aria-labelledby id resolving against a hidden duplicate page root (the #093 failure mode visibleByTestId exists for), or the bare focus() at tools-search-results-page.tsx:470 scrolling late. NEITHER IS PROVEN. Why: Why it matters - if the click genuinely no-ops, a Firefox user cannot page through document search hits at all, which is a clinical reading path; if it double-fires it is a harness artefact and the test should assert the active chunk id rather than a modulo-2 counter. Context: Six Firefox failures in main run 35503893104; four fixed in PRs #2932 and #2933, these two left. Parent row #9Z197J. Owner: unknown - depends on what the trace shows. Confidence: high that the cause is shared and not CSS/text-matching; low on any single mechanism. Depends on: the egress row - the trace could not be downloaded from the cloud container.
